q: Under Sec. 27.2, it is imperative that a PCA secure which of the following, commensurate with the magnitude and scope of project involvement?
o: A Professional Liability Insurance Policy, professional indemnity insurance, or equivalent bond
A foreign currency bank account
A personal life insurance policy naming the Client as beneficiary
A separate business permit for each project
n: Sec. 27.2 requires the PCA to secure a Professional Liability Insurance Policy, professional indemnity insurance, or an equivalent bond, commensurate with the project's magnitude, scope, and corresponding compensation; its cost forms part of the total project cost chargeable to the Client. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 27.2)

q: Under Sec. 19.10 of SPP Document 209, which of the following is classified as a "Direct Cost or Reimbursable Expense" rather than "Overhead"?
o: Business development expenses of the firm in general
Office rent and air-conditioning for the working space
Identifiable long-distance telephone, internet, and courier/postage expenses directly related to the project
Executive and administrative salaries not identifiable to a specific project
n: Sec. 19.10.2 lists identifiable communication expenses (long-distance telephone, telegraph, internet, SMS, cable, express charge, postage) as Direct Costs/Reimbursable Expenses, distinct from Overhead items like office space, general administrative salaries, and business development expenses (Sec. 19.14). (Source: SPP Document 209, Secs. 19.10.2, 19.14)

q: Under Sec. 23, a Professional Consulting Architect (PCA) may provide PACS to the Client:
o: Only directly, never through a firm
Only via an accredited foreign partner firm
Only through a government agency as intermediary
Directly or indirectly, in the manner prescribed, suggested or promulgated by the Commission/Board through the IAPOA
n: Sec. 23 provides that a PCA may provide services directly or indirectly to the Client, in the manner prescribed, suggested, or promulgated by the Commission/Board through the IAPOA. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 23)

q: Under Sec. 30 (Penalty Clause and Sanction), a person who engages in PACS without being qualified under R.A. No. 9266 and its IRR shall be subject to:
o: Sanction/s by appropriate public or private entities, without prejudice to filing of criminal, civil, administrative or special complaints
Automatic revocation of any unrelated business permit
No penalty, since PACS is a purely voluntary standard
A warning letter only, with no further consequence
n: Sec. 30 provides that anyone who engages in PACS without the qualifications prescribed under R.A. No. 9266 and its IRR shall be subject to sanction/s by appropriate public or private entities, without prejudice to filing criminal, civil, administrative or special complaints. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 30)

q: Under Sec. 19.12, one of the requirements for a "Foreign Consultant (FC)/Foreign Architect (FA)" is that the individual must have secured a temporary/special permit (TSP) implementing which sections of R.A. No. 9266?
o: Secs. 9184 and 9285
Secs. 37 and 38
Secs. 14 and 15
Secs. 20 and 33
n: Sec. 19.12.2 requires the FC/FA to have acquired a temporary/special permit (TSP) to practice architecture on Philippine soil in accordance with Board Resolutions implementing Secs. 37 and 38 of R.A. No. 9266. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.12.2)

q: Under Sec. 24.7.1 (Per Diem or Hourly Basis), this compensation method is particularly suited to engagements involving:
o: Only government projects covered by R.A. No. 9184
Intermittent personal service, with the PCA compensated for all time devoted to the work, including travel time
Only very large, long-duration infrastructure projects
Projects where the total cost cannot ever be estimated
n: Sec. 24.7.1 states the Per Diem or Hourly Basis method suits engagements involving intermittent personal service, compensating the PCA for all time devoted to the work, including travel time, plus reimbursement of related out-of-pocket expenses. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.1)

q: Which statement best captures how SPP Document 209 relates to other professional-practice issuances governing architecture?
o: It operates independently of R.A. No. 9266 and is not an IRR of any law
It applies only to foreign consultants and has no bearing on Filipino architects
It repeals and replaces all prior SPP documents and the CES entirely
It is meant to complement R.A. No. 9266, the IP Code, the GPRA, the CES and other SPPs, without unduly affecting them
n: Sec. 16.8 clarifies that the SPP on PACS is meant to complement existing PRLs, the IP Code, the GPRA, the CES and other SPPs, and that nothing in it must unduly affect those laws, policies, rules, regulations, the CES, and other SPPs. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 16.8)

q: According to Sec. 19.13, the "multiplier" used in PACS fee computation varies according to:
o: The floor area of the project only
The nationality of the Client only
The number of years since the PCA passed the licensure exam only
The type of architectural consulting work, the organization/experience of the PCA, and the geographic area of the PCA's office
n: Sec. 19.13 states the multiplier varies according to the types of architectural consulting work, the PCA's organization and experience, and the geographic area where the office is located. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.13)

q: Under Sec. 24.7.4 (Fixed/Lump Sum payment), which sub-method is described as "direct development of a fixed amount of compensation by estimating the individual elements of the cost outlines, plus a reasonable margin of profit"?
o: The Retainer method
Sub-method (a)
The Percentage of Total Project Cost method (Sec. 24.7.5)
Sub-method (b)
n: Sec. 24.7.4(b) describes direct development of a fixed lump-sum amount by estimating individual cost-outline elements plus a reasonable profit margin, as distinct from sub-method (a), which computes the lump sum as a percentage of estimated total project cost. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.4(b))

q: Following LoI No. 1000, which two organizations initiated the preparation of the original "Standard Guidelines on Consultancy/Consulting Services"?
o: The Philippine Federation of Professional Associations (PFPA) and the Philippine Technological Council (PTC)
The PRC and the UAP
The CBNE and the DTI
The IAPOA and the PRBoA
n: The PFPA (umbrella organization of PRC-accredited professional associations) and the PTC (then composed of 14 accredited technological APOs) initiated the original guidelines document. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 15.2)

q: Under Sec. 19.16, in the specific context of PACS, the term "Accredited Professional Organization (APO)" refers specifically to:
o: The IAPOA
The Philippine Federation of Professional Associations (PFPA)
The PRC as a whole
The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
n: Sec. 19.16 states that while APO generally covers organizations under the CBNE/PTC umbrella, for PACS purposes the term specifically refers to the IAPOA. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.16)

q: Under Sec. 24.8, fees for services requiring artistic, innovative and creative input shall be determined:
o: Only through the Per Diem/Hourly method
Differently from services involving purely technical and scientific undertakings
At a rate lower than technical services in all cases
In exactly the same manner as purely technical/scientific services
n: Sec. 24.8 states that fees for artistic, innovative and creative services shall not be determined in the same manner as fees for purely technical and scientific undertakings. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.8)

q: What is stated as the primary purpose of the SPP for Professional Architectural Consulting Services (PACS)?
o: To complement existing professional regulatory laws governing architecture and other pertinent laws, without unduly affecting them
To replace R.A. No. 9266 entirely
To set uniform government salary scales for all licensed architects
To abolish the practice of consulting by foreign architects
n: Sec. 16.8 states the SPP's primary purpose is to complement R.A. No. 9266, the IP Code (R.A. 8293), the GPRA (R.A. 9184), the CES, other SPPs, and related regulations, and that nothing in it must unduly affect those laws and issuances. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 16.8)

q: Under Sec. 19.20, "Salary Cost" of professional consultants includes the cost of salaries (including sick leave, vacation, holiday and incentive pay) for time chargeable to the project, plus:
o: Excise and payroll taxes, other imposable taxes/duties, and contributions for social security and insurance benefits
The Client's own project financing costs
Reimbursable direct costs of the project
The firm's general marketing budget
n: Sec. 19.20 defines Salary Cost as including chargeable salaries plus excise/payroll and other imposable taxes/duties and contributions for social security and insurance benefits. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.20)

q: Given the scenario, which compensation method under Sec. 24.7 of SPP Document 209 is most appropriate, and why?
o: Salary Cost times a Multiplier, plus Direct Cost/Reimbursable Expenses — because it best suits projects with hard-to-pre-determine costs and possible scope-altering investigative work
Retainer — because the firm expects to be on call over a long period
Per Diem or Hourly Basis — because it is the only method that reimburses travel expenses
Percentage of Total Project Cost — because it is simplest to apply to any project
n: Sec. 24.7.3 states the Salary Cost x Multiplier + Direct Cost method is best suited for projects for which costs are difficult to pre-determine, or where additional investigative work may further alter the project's scope — exactly the scenario described. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.3)
scenario: A five-person team of PCAs and staff at a Registered Architectural Firm (RAF) is engaged for a mixed-use development whose costs are difficult to pre-determine at the outset, and additional investigative work may still alter the project's scope. The team's total basic Salary Cost chargeable to the project is PHP 500,000. The firm's Direct Costs/Reimbursable Expenses for the engagement total PHP 150,000.

q: Per the Objectives (Sec. 17.1) of SPP Document 209, a basic legal precondition for anyone to be a Professional Consulting Architect (PCA) is that they must first be:
o: An employee of a government agency
A holder of a master's degree in architecture
A registered and licensed Architect (RLA)
A member of a foreign professional institute
n: Sec. 17.1 states that by law, PCAs must first be registered and licensed Architects (RLAs), on which basis standards are built to develop their competencies, credibility and integrity. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 17.1)

q: Under Sec. 20, which of the following activities is included within the scope of PACS?
o: Adjudicating criminal cases in court
Certifying food and drug safety
Issuing currency regulations
Teaching, lecturing, coaching and mentoring
n: Sec. 20.4 explicitly lists teaching, lecturing, coaching, mentoring as within the scope of PACS. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 20.4)

q: In the scenario, Sec. 24.7.4 further requires that, aside from stating the fee, the lump-sum agreement must also clearly provide for:
o: A waiver of the PCA's right to seal the documents
Exemption of the PCA from all professional liability
Automatic conversion to a Per Diem arrangement after the first year
A stated time limit for performing the services and additional compensation for extra time used
n: Sec. 24.7.4 requires lump-sum agreements to contain a clearly stated time limit for the services and a provision for additional compensation for extra time used, plus clarity on where final approval authority lies. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.4)
scenario: An Owner engages a PCA for a residential subdivision project whose scope of PACS can be clearly and fully defined at the outset. The parties agree to compute the fee under Sec. 24.7.4(a) of SPP Document 209 (a lump-sum computed as an appropriate percentage of the estimated total project cost). The estimated total project cost is PHP 20,000,000, and the parties agree on a rate of 6% of that cost as the lump-sum compensation.

q: Under Sec. 18.2 of SPP Document 209, adherence by State-registered and licensed professionals (RLPs) such as RLAs to their respective SPPs is described as:
o: Optional and only recommended
Applicable only to government-employed architects
Mandatory
Waivable upon written request to the Commission
n: Sec. 18.2 states it "shall be mandatory" upon all RLPs, such as RLAs, to strictly adhere to their respective SPPs within the bounds of their profession's scope of practice. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 18.2)

q: Under Sec. 21.2, a juridical-person PCA (a consulting firm) must, in addition to SEC or DTI registration, also possess:
o: A certificate of good standing from a foreign chamber of commerce
A separate license from the Department of Foreign Affairs
A valid Commission certificate to operate as a Registered Architectural Firm (RAF)
A minimum paid-up capital of PHP 10,000,000
n: Sec. 21.2 requires the consulting firm, in addition to SEC/DTI registration, to possess a valid Commission certificate to operate as a Registered Architectural Firm (RAF). (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 21.2)

q: Under Sec. 26, duplicating or copying a PCA's architectural documents for use on other/repeat projects requires:
o: The written consent of the PCA or author of the said documents
A separate government copyright registration in every instance
Only the Commission's approval, without the PCA's consent
No consent at all, as long as the Client paid for the original project
n: Sec. 26 provides that no person, without the written consent of the PCA/author, shall duplicate or copy such documents for use in repetition of, or for other, projects, whether executed partly or in entirety. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 26)

q: Under SPP Document 209, a "Consulting Agreement" is best described as:
o: A government permit required before an architect may practice
An informal verbal understanding requiring no documentation
A certificate proving membership in the IAPOA

A binding covenant between a PCA/consulting firm (RAF) and an Owner/Client setting the mutually agreed terms and conditions for the specific work, study or joint venture requiring special/technical skills
n: Sec. 19.6 defines a Consulting Agreement as a binding covenant or understanding between a PCA and/or consulting firm (RAF) and an Owner/Client that sets out mutually agreed terms and conditions under which the specific work requiring special/technical skills shall be undertaken. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.6)

q: A private developer wants to engage a foreign architect (FA) for a CBNE-covered specialization, but no qualified Filipino Professional Consulting Architect (FPCA) is available in that field. Under Sec. 22.2, what must the developer additionally do?
o: Employ at least ten (10) Filipino architects as understudies
Secure written approval from the President of the Philippines
Nothing further is required once no FPCA is available
Employ a minimum of two (2) Filipino RLAs in the same field of specialization as understudies
n: Sec. 22.2 provides that where no qualified FPCA is available and a non-FPCA (FA/FC) is engaged, a minimum of two (2) Filipino RLAs in the same field of specialization shall be employed as understudies. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 22.2)

q: Under Sec. 28 (Applicability), the SPP for PACS shall be adopted by the IAPOA, which shall thereafter formulate:
o: A separate licensure examination for PACS practitioners
The covering guidelines and Manual of Procedure (MoP)
A new professional regulatory law to supersede R.A. No. 9266
A national building code amendment
n: Sec. 28 states this SPP shall be adopted by the IAPOA, which shall thereafter formulate the covering guidelines and Manual of Procedure (MoP). (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 28)

q: Under the definition of "Filipino Professional Consulting Architect (FPCA)" in SPP Document 209, an FPCA who signs and seals architectural documents thereby becomes:
o: An Architect-of-record (AOR), assuming the attendant professional responsibilities and civil liabilities
Automatically a member of the PRBoA
A Foreign Consultant for purposes of that project
Exempt from continuing professional education requirements
n: Sec. 19.11 states that if the FPCA signs and seals architectural documents, he becomes an Architect-of-record (AOR) for the project and assumes the attendant professional responsibilities and civil liabilities. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.11)

q: Under Sec. 24.2, how should compensation be treated for PACS requiring more than one type of expertise/specialization, compared to those requiring only one kind?
o: Multi-expertise PACS may not be compensated under this SPP at all
Identically in all cases, with no distinction allowed
Multi-expertise PACS must always be compensated at a lower rate
Differently — compensation for single-expertise/related-expertise PACS is treated differently from multi-expertise PACS
n: Sec. 24.2 states that compensation for PACS requiring only one kind of expertise (or related types) shall be treated differently from those requiring more than one type of expertise. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.2)

q: SPP Document 209 was approved on 27 July 2010 as a supplemental IRR of which law?
o: R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004)
R.A. No. 9285 (the ADR Act of 2004)
R.A. No. 8293 (the IP Code of the Philippines)
R.A. No. 9184 (the GPRA of 2003)
n: The footer of every page of SPP Document 209 (part of the 2010 Standards of Professional Practice) states it was "Approved 27 July 2010 as the Supplemental IRR of R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004)." (Source: SPP Document 209, page footer)

q: Under Sec. 19.12, a Foreign Consultant (FC) must, among other requirements, be:
o: A citizen of an ASEAN member-state only
Sponsored personally by the Commission Chairperson
Exempt from securing any Philippine government permit
A registered and/or licensed professional architect in his own country of origin (and/or country of residence/practice, as applicable)
n: Sec. 19.12.4 requires the FC/FA to be a registered and/or licensed professional architect in his own country of origin (and/or country of residence/practice). (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.12.4)

q: Under Sec. 24.7.2 (Retainer), this method of remuneration is used when:
o: The Client wants to pay strictly per square meter of floor area
The PCA will render services only once, for a single fixed task
The project cost cannot be estimated under any circumstance
The PCA's services are expected to be required at intervals over a period of time, ensuring availability to the Client when needed
n: Sec. 24.7.2 explains the Retainer method is used when the PCA's services are expected to be required at intervals over time, ensuring in advance that his services will be available to the Client when required. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.2)

q: SPP Document 209 (Professional Architectural Consulting Services) officially replaces which earlier document?
o: The 1981 UAP Document 210
UAP Document 200
SPP Document 208
The 2004 IRR of R.A. No. 9266
n: The title page of SPP Document 209 states it is "(replacing the 1981 UAP Doc. 210)." (Source: SPP Document 209, title page)

q: Under Sec. 19.14, which item is classified as part of "Overhead" rather than a project's Direct Cost/Reimbursable Expense?
o: Blue-printing and reproduction costs applicable to the work
Depreciation allowances or rental of furniture, equipment and instruments of the office
Special consultants' fees directly applicable to the contracted work
Long-distance telephone charges identifiable to the project
n: Sec. 19.14.2 classifies depreciation allowances or rental of office furniture, equipment and instruments as Overhead, distinct from the project-specific Direct Costs listed under Sec. 19.10. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.14.2)

q: Under Sec. 24.7.4, when compensation is on a lump-sum basis, the agreement should clearly state:
o: That no time limit ever applies to lump-sum agreements
A time limit for performance of the service/s, plus provision for additional compensation for extra time used
That the fee is payable only after project completion, with no interim payments
That the PCA waives any right to additional compensation regardless of scope changes
n: Sec. 24.7.4 states lump-sum agreements should contain a clearly stated time limit for performing the services, with provision for additional compensation for extra time used, and clarity on where final design-approval authority lies. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.4)

q: The amended (2010) version of the Standard Guidelines on Consulting Services embodied in SPP Document 209 was based on a document jointly drafted by the PTC and which other body, pursuant to a Joint Resolution dated December 11, 2009?
o: The Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA)
The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
The Council for the Built and Natural Environments (CBNE)
The Professional Regulation Commission (PRC)
n: The amended version is based on the document jointly drafted by the PTC and the Council for the Built and Natural Environments (CBNE), per their Joint Resolution No. 2009-01 dated December 11, 2009. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 15.5)

q: Sec. 19.17 defines "Professional Architectural Consulting Services (PACS)" as the rendering, by a PCA or a consulting firm (RAF), of:
o: Only the sale of architectural plans to the public

Independent advice, extension of technical assistance and services, and undertaking of activities requiring appropriate knowledge, skills, training, experience, competence, integrity and/or financial and logistical capability
Only teaching activities at accredited architecture schools
Only the physical construction of buildings
n: Sec. 19.17 defines PACS as the rendering by a PCA or a consulting firm (RAF) of independent advice, technical assistance/services, and activities requiring appropriate knowledge, skills, training, experience, recognized competence, integrity, and/or financial and logistical capability. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.17)

q: Under Sec. 24.9, who is responsible for promulgating, approving and adopting the criteria for establishing the method(s) of PACS compensation?
o: The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas
The IAPOA
The Client, on a purely unilateral basis
The Department of Budget and Management
n: Sec. 24.9 states the criteria for establishing method/s of compensation shall be promulgated, approved and adopted by the IAPOA. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.9)

q: According to the Rationale, full utilization of Filipino Professional Consultants (FPCs) chiefly helps the country by:
o: Eliminating the need for professional regulatory boards
Reducing the need for continuing professional education
Increasing the number of foreign consultants allowed to practice
Minimizing importation of foreign expertise and the resulting expenditure of foreign exchange
n: Sec. 16.4 states that full utilization of FPCs can minimize the importation of foreign expertise, which entails considerable expenditure of hard-earned foreign exchange. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 16.4)

q: Under Sec. 20 of SPP Document 209, the scope of PACS is defined and determined in accordance with the charter, by-laws, policies, rules and regulations of the Commission and the Board through which body?
o: The IAPOA
The PFPA
The Bureau of Immigration
The DTI
n: Sec. 20 states the scope of PACS is defined per the charter, by-laws, policies, rules and regulations of the Commission and the Board through the IAPOA to which the PCA belongs. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 20)

q: Using the formula given in Sec. 24.7.3 (Fee = Salary Cost x Multiplier + Reimbursable Expenses) and the SPP's stated multiplier factor of 3.0, what is the total fee for the engagement in the scenario?
n: Fee = (PHP 500,000 x 3.0) + PHP 150,000 = PHP 1,500,000 + PHP 150,000 = PHP 1,650,000. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.3 (formula: Fee = Salary Cost x Multiplier + Reimbursable Expenses; multiplier factor of 3.0))
scenario: A five-person team of PCAs and staff at a Registered Architectural Firm (RAF) is engaged for a mixed-use development whose costs are difficult to pre-determine at the outset, and additional investigative work may still alter the project's scope. The team's total basic Salary Cost chargeable to the project is PHP 500,000. The firm's Direct Costs/Reimbursable Expenses for the engagement total PHP 150,000.

q: One stated Objective (Sec. 17.3) of the SPP is to ensure compliance with advisories on engaging foreign architects/consultants in order to:
o: Give foreign consultants priority over RLAs in government projects
Stimulate the local market for Filipino professional consultants and level the field of practice between RLAs and FAs/FCs
Completely ban foreign consultants from the Philippines
Exempt foreign consultants from securing any permit to practice
n: Sec. 17.3 aims at full compliance with guidelines on engaging foreign architects/consultants as a measure to stimulate the local market for RLA-PCAs and protect/level the field between RLAs and FAs/FCs. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 17.3)

q: Sec. 20.16 lists which of the following as the last enumerated item within the scope of PACS?
o: Marketing and promotional studies
Capital Investment Programming
Site selection, analyses, evaluation, ranking and development
Land use and multi-sectoral development planning
n: Sec. 20.16, the final item in the Sec. 20 enumeration, is "Capital Investment Programming." (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 20.16)

q: Under Sec. 25 (Seal and Use of Seal under PACS), a PCA shall sign and affix his professional license number and Commission/Board/IAPOA-approved seal on architectural documents and deliverables prepared by him or under his direct supervision, if and only if:
o: The Client specifically requests it in writing
The project is government-funded
The document is submitted for a foreign competition
The PCA shall also act as the Architect-of-record (Aor), assuming all attendant professional responsibilities and civil liabilities for the project
n: Sec. 25 conditions the sealing of documents on the PCA also acting as Architect-of-record (Aor), in which case he assumes all attendant professional responsibilities and civil liabilities for the project. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 25)

q: Under SPP Document 209, "Comprehensive Development" is defined as:
o: A synonym for "project cost"
The construction of high-rise buildings in urban centers only
The process of registering an architectural firm with the SEC
The holistic and progressive growth and advancement of a community, province, region and nation across economic, social, physical, environmental and institutional sectors
n: Sec. 19.1 defines Comprehensive Development as the holistic and progressive growth of a community, province, region and nation, inclusive of its economic, social, physical, environmental and institutional sectors. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.1)

q: Under Sec. 21.5, one of the qualifications a PCA must possess is that he/she:
o: Must be at least 50 years old
Must hold a doctorate degree
Has never been convicted of any criminal or administrative offense related to deliberate wrongdoing
Must have practiced abroad for at least 5 years
n: Sec. 21.5 requires that the PCA has never been convicted of any criminal or administrative offense related to deliberate wrongdoing. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 21.5)

q: Under Sec. 27.1, any individual, partner, firm/corporation/consortium or joint venture engaged in PACS is:
o: Liable only to the Client and to no one else
Professionally responsible before the State and civilly liable before the State, the general public, and the Client, for the conduct and performance of his/her services
Immune from any liability once the project is completed
Liable only for criminal, never civil, consequences
n: Sec. 27.1 states that anyone engaged in PACS is legally/professionally responsible before the State and civilly liable before the State, the general public, and the Client, for the conduct and performance of services rendered. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 27.1)

q: A "Consulting Architectural Firm (CAF)" under Sec. 19.7 must be registered with which agencies, in addition to the Commission/Board?
o: The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) only
The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), or the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) for a sole proprietorship
The Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) only
The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP)
n: Sec. 19.7 defines a CAF as a corporation/association/group/partnership registered with the SEC, or a sole proprietorship registered with the DTI, and likewise registered with the Commission/Board. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.7)

q: Under Sec. 22.3, the selection of PCAs for Government projects shall be in accordance with the relevant provisions of:
o: R.A. No. 9266 alone, with no reference to procurement law
R.A. No. 9184 (the Government Procurement Reform Act of 2003)
R.A. No. 9285 (the ADR Act of 2004)
R.A. No. 8293 (the Intellectual Property Code)
n: Sec. 22.3 requires that selection of PCAs for Government projects follow the relevant provisions of R.A. No. 9184, the Government Procurement Reform Act (GPRA) of 2003. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 22.3)

q: Under Sec. 29 (Alternative Dispute Resolution), disputes arising from the IRR's implementation shall be resolved through ADR modes mandated under R.A. No. 9285, which must necessarily include:
o: Only arbitration, to the exclusion of all other modes
Negotiation, conciliation, mediation and arbitration
Administrative complaint before the PRC only
Direct court litigation only
n: Sec. 29 requires that ADR modes under R.A. No. 9285 (the ADR Act of 2004) be used before referral to a competent court, and that these must necessarily include negotiation, conciliation, mediation and arbitration; an ADR clause must form part of all PACS agreements. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 29)

q: Under Sec. 19.11, aside from being a Philippine citizen and a natural person, an FPCA must also be:
o: An employee of a government agency
A holder of a foreign architectural license
A Philippine-registered and licensed architect (RLA) and a member in good standing of the IAPOA
A graduate of a foreign architecture school
n: Sec. 19.11 requires the FPCA to be a Philippine-registered and licensed architect (RLA), a member in good standing of the IAPOA, and specializing in a State-regulated branch of architecture under R.A. No. 9266. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.11)

q: Under Sec. 24.4, for the same scope of work, SPP Document 209 requires that compensation between Filipino PCAs (FPCAs) and their foreign consultant (FC) counterparts:
o: Shall always favor FCs by at least 20%
Shall have no disparity
Shall always favor FPCAs by a fixed multiplier
Is left entirely to informal negotiation with no guiding principle
n: Sec. 24.4 explicitly states there shall be no disparity in compensation between FPCAs and their FC counterparts for the same scope of work. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.4)

q: Which of the following best identifies who is authorized to render Professional Architectural Consulting Services (PACS) under SPP Document 209?
o: Any individual who has completed a short online course in architecture
Any foreign national holding a tourist visa
A Professional Consulting Architect (PCA) or a Registered Architectural Firm (RAF), including Filipino Professional Consulting Architects (FPCAs), acting within their qualifications
Any construction contractor licensed by the DTI
n: Throughout SPP Document 209 (Secs. 19.11, 19.15, 19.17, 21), PACS is rendered by qualified PCAs (natural persons who are RLAs and IAPOA members in good standing) or by RAFs (juridical persons meeting SEC/DTI and Commission requirements), including FPCAs. (Source: SPP Document 209, Secs. 19.11, 19.15, 19.17, 21)

q: The "Multiplier" defined in Sec. 19.13 of SPP Document 209 compensates the PCA for all of the following EXCEPT:
o: Direct construction cost of the project
Fringe benefits and social charges
Fee for contingencies, interest on capital reserves, and profit
Overhead costs of the office
n: Sec. 19.13 lists the multiplier's components as overhead costs, fringe benefits/social charges, fee for contingencies, interest on capital reserves, and profit — not the direct construction cost of the project. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.13)

q: Under Sec. 24.7.3, the "Salary Cost times a Multiplier, plus Direct Cost" method is best suited for projects where:
o: The Client insists on a lump-sum fee regardless of scope changes
Only per diem-eligible personal services are involved
Costs are difficult to pre-determine, or additional experimental/investigative work may be needed that could further alter the project's scope
The total project cost is already fixed and fully known in advance
n: Sec. 24.7.3 states this method is best suited for projects whose costs are difficult to pre-determine, or where additional experimental or investigative work may be needed that could further alter the project's scope. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.3)

q: Letter of Instruction (LoI) No. 1000, cited in the Foreword of SPP Document 209, was issued on March 20, 1980 by which President, and directed what?
o: Fidel V. Ramos; adoption of the Architecture Act
Corazon C. Aquino; the creation of the PRC
Ferdinand E. Marcos; government agencies to give priority to APO members in hiring and engagement of professional services
Ferdinand E. Marcos; the creation of the PRBoA
n: LoI No. 1000 was issued by then-President Ferdinand E. Marcos, directing all government agencies and instrumentalities to give priority to members of accredited professional organizations (APOs) in hiring and in engaging professional services. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 15.1)

q: Under Sec. 19.15, a "Professional Consulting Architect (PCA)" must, among other things, hold:
o: A driver's license issued in the Philippines
A valid registration certification and Commission ID card, and be a member in good standing of the IAPOA
A business permit from the local government unit only
A postgraduate degree from a foreign university
n: Sec. 19.15 requires the PCA to be a Philippine-registered and licensed Architect (RLA) with a valid registration certification and Commission ID card, and a member in good standing of the IAPOA. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.15)

q: Under Sec. 24.7.5, the validity of the "Percentage of Total Project Cost" method rests on the assumption that:
o: Only government projects may use a percentage-based fee
The percentage used must always exceed 20% of project cost
Consultancy costs are always fixed regardless of project cost
Consultancy costs vary in proportion to the total project cost, regardless of the type or location of the project
n: Sec. 24.7.5 states the method's validity rests on the assumption that consultancy costs vary in proportion to total project cost, regardless of project type or location, and should be applied only where experience shows an approximate correlation. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.5)

q: What prompted the 2010 re-visiting of the original 1981 guidelines, according to the Foreword of SPP Document 209?
o: A directive from the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture to renumber all SPP documents
A shortage of licensed architects in the Philippines
The influx of foreign consultants and the proliferation of unqualified entities calling themselves "consultants"
The passage of the Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines
n: The Foreword explains that three decades after 1981, it became urgent to revisit the document because of the influx of foreign consultants and the rise of entities projecting themselves as "consultants" without adequate skills, training or experience. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 15.4)

q: Under Sec. 19.18, "Project Cost" means the total cost of the project, which includes but is not limited to:
o: Only government permit and licensing fees
Only the architect's professional fee
Construction cost, fees for professional services, cost of land/right-of-way (ROW), and legal/administrative and other related expenses of the client
Only the cost of construction materials
n: Sec. 19.18 defines Project Cost as the total project cost including but not limited to construction cost, professional fees, cost of land/ROW, and legal, administrative and other related client expenses. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.18)

q: Under Sec. 24.10, unless otherwise mutually agreed with the Client, a PCA is entitled to interest — at the prevailing rate set by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) plus an IAPOA-determined percentage — on fees and other charges that remain unpaid:
o: Beyond 90 days from contract signing
Beyond 7 days from project completion
Beyond 30 days from receipt of billing
Immediately upon issuance of any billing, with no grace period
n: Sec. 24.10 grants the PCA interest at the BSP prevailing rate plus an IAPOA-determined percentage on fees, other charges, and reimbursements not paid within 30 days from receipt of billing, unless otherwise mutually agreed. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.10)

q: The Rationale (Sec. 16.5) argues that the presence of foreign architects in the Philippines is problematic mainly because:
o: Foreign architects charge lower fees than Filipino architects
Foreign architects are exempt from all Philippine taxes
Foreign architects are legally barred from practicing in the Philippines under any circumstance
The "technology transfer" they claim to bring is already adequately available locally, yet they compete on terms adverse to and displace Filipino RLPs
n: Sec. 16.5 explains that the technology foreign consultants claim to transfer is often already available in adequate proportion locally, so their presence instead displaces Filipino Professional Consultants (FPCs) from significant projects. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 16.5)

q: Which of the following is explicitly listed under Sec. 20 as within the scope of Professional Architectural Consulting Services (PACS)?
o: Setting national tax policy
Pre-investment/pre-feasibility and feasibility studies
Regulating banking interest rates
Issuing government building permits
n: Sec. 20.7 lists "conduct of pre-investment/pre-feasibility and feasibility studies" among the scope items of PACS. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 20.7)

q: Under the scenario, what lump-sum fee results from applying Sec. 24.7.4(a)'s percentage-of-project-cost approach?
n: Lump-sum fee = 6% x PHP 20,000,000 = PHP 1,200,000, computed as a percentage of the estimated total project cost per Sec. 24.7.4(a). (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.4(a))
scenario: An Owner engages a PCA for a residential subdivision project whose scope of PACS can be clearly and fully defined at the outset. The parties agree to compute the fee under Sec. 24.7.4(a) of SPP Document 209 (a lump-sum computed as an appropriate percentage of the estimated total project cost). The estimated total project cost is PHP 20,000,000, and the parties agree on a rate of 6% of that cost as the lump-sum compensation.

q: SPP Document 209's Declaration of Policy quotes Section 14, Article XII of the 1987 Constitution, which provides that the practice of all professions in the Philippines shall be:
o: Open to any foreign national holding a work visa
Subject to a uniform national licensing fee regardless of profession
Regulated solely by private professional associations
Limited to Filipino citizens, save in cases prescribed by law
n: Sec. 18.1 quotes Sec. 14, Art. XII of the 1987 Constitution: "The practice of all professions in the Philippines shall be limited to Filipino citizens, save in cases prescribed by law." (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 18.1 (1987 Constitution, Art. XII, Sec. 14))

q: Under Sec. 21.1, if a Professional Consulting Architect (PCA) is a natural person, he/she must be:
o: A person who has passed the bar examination
A citizen of the Philippines, a duly registered/licensed Architect (RLA), holder of a valid Commission ID card-license, and a member in good standing of the IAPOA
A holder of a foreign architecture license only
Any registered engineer regardless of citizenship
n: Sec. 21.1 requires the natural-person PCA to be a Filipino citizen who is a duly registered and licensed Architect, holding a valid Commission ID card-license and IAPOA good standing. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 21.1)

q: Under Sec. 26 (Intellectual Property Rights for PACS), architectural documentary outputs by a PCA are protected under which provisions of R.A. No. 9266 and its IRR?
o: Secs. 37 and 38
Secs. 24 and 25
Secs. 20(4) and 33
Secs. 14 and 15
n: Sec. 26 states such outputs and materials are protected under Secs. 20(4) and 33 of R.A. No. 9266 and its 2004 IRR, whether executed or not. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 26)

q: A "Consortium or Association" under Sec. 19.2 of SPP Document 209 refers to:
o: A trade union of construction workers
Any two Filipino architects sharing an office space
A coalition of purely Filipino professional consultants/firms, or Filipino consultants/firms in collaboration with foreign consultants/firms authorized to render such services
A government agency that regulates architectural practice
n: Sec. 19.2 defines Consortium or Association as a coalition of purely Filipino RLA-PCAs/RAFs, or such Filipino consultants/firms in collaboration with foreign consultants/firms authorized to render consulting services. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.2)

q: Under Sec. 22.1, the major consideration in hiring a Professional Consulting Architect (PCA) is stated to be:
o: Personal familiarity with the Client
Nationality of the PCA's alma mater
The lowest possible fee quoted
His/her qualifications, such as competence, capabilities and integrity
n: Sec. 22.1 states the major consideration in hiring a PCA is his/her qualifications as provided in the SPP — competence, capabilities and integrity. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 22.1)
